title: Crypto retreats as Bitcoin ETF inflows rebound and ARC weighs on the portfolio
paragraphs: Bitcoin fell 1.04% over 24 hours to about $81,450, while ether lost 1.50% to $2,384. The pullback extended across crypto: CoinDesk reported its broad CD80 index down 0.34% and its DeFi index down 1.2%, reversing part of the previous session's recovery.

Asian equities also weakened. South Korea's Kospi fell 3.73%, with chipmakers under pressure amid concerns about AI spending, while Nasdaq 100 futures slipped. Brent crude near $110 adds an inflation risk. This is a difficult backdrop for speculative assets, although those simultaneous moves do not establish a single cause for crypto's decline.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs attracted $526.6 million in their latest session, the strongest daily total in nearly a month. BlackRock's IBIT brought in $665.2 million, more than offsetting withdrawals from Fidelity and Grayscale. Ether ETFs instead lost $103.3 million, their fourth consecutive session of outflows. The contrast matters: a strong Bitcoin headline masks concentrated buying and continued weakness in demand for ether funds.

Coinbase and Thunes announced a partnership connecting stablecoin infrastructure with payouts into bank accounts and mobile wallets. Coinbase will integrate Thunes' network, while supplying the stablecoin technology for Thunes. Supplier payments, gig-worker earnings and remittances are among the intended uses. The practical opportunity is to make digital dollars easier to receive through familiar local payment systems. The announcement does not specify a launch schedule or initial country coverage.

Zerohash launched AUTH, which lets users link exchange accounts and self-custody wallets, then authorize transfers without manually copying addresses or choosing networks. The company advertises more than 600 connections, largely wallets; its documentation says each transfer requires user approval and participating apps control permitted assets and accounts. This could reduce transfer errors and setup friction. Its reach will depend on which connections and transfers individual platforms actually enable.

Our on-chain portfolio is about $75,850: $11,200 in the active treasury and $64,650 in the cold-storage Safe. Its marked value fell $5,122, or 6.3%, from the previous verified edition. The Safe's 26.74 million directly held ARC is unchanged in quantity but fell about $4,363 in value to $50,973. That holding represents 67% of the portfolio, with further ARC exposure in the Safe's $10,491 WETH/ARC liquidity pool. ARC concentration remains the largest portfolio risk.

The treasury also holds about $3,465 in Beefy pools and $2,484 in cbETH. Combined net Aave value is roughly $5,010, down $129. Visible lending debt totals about $4,196; Aave health factors eased from 2.50 to 2.46 in the treasury and from 1.99 to 1.96 in the Safe. Fluid has $1,213 supplied against $1,060 borrowed and a health factor of 1.03, leaving a narrow liquidation cushion despite its small $153 net value.
